title: Return a shopping trolley: push the chain key of the trolley in front home in your coin lock, then take the quarter back
instruction: Return the shopping trolley: take the key hanging on its chain from the coin lock of the trolley in front, push it fully into the key slot of your trolley's coin lock, then take out the quarter the lock releases and lay it on the rubber mat. Leave the key in the lock and take both hands away.
context: Supermarket coin-lock trolleys are returned by coupling them: the chain key of the trolley in front goes into the returned trolley's lock, which then releases the deposit coin. The key hangs loose on a chain and must be found, gripped, turned and lined up with a narrow slot among the tubes of two nested trolleys.
setup: World x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, heights over the bench top. Two nested trolleys shown by their push handles, both steel tube 25 mm across: a straight handle 300 mm long along y (y -0.10 to 0.20), its axis 0.340 m over the bench, with a side tube at each end running 80 mm forward (+x) and down to the bench. The near (returned) trolley's handle is at x 0.150, the front trolley's handle 178 mm further on at x 0.328. Each handle carries a coin lock (grey plastic body, 90 mm along the handle, 70 mm across, 68 mm tall, red top; on the handle, centred at y 0.05). The near lock has a 21 x 4.5 mm key slot in its front (+x) face, centred at y 0.02, 0.364 m over the bench, and holds a US quarter (24.26 mm, 1.75 mm thick, 5.67 g) out of sight in its coin slide. From the back face of each lock a steel chain of 11 links of 20 mm (220 mm) hangs free. On the front lock's chain hangs its key, a flat steel tag 62 x 15 x 3 mm (22 g) with a 9 mm wide hole from 6 to 14 mm behind its tip, tip down, its line at x 0.290, y 0.020, its tip 66.5 mm over the bench, broad faces facing x. The near lock's chain carries the same key, its line at x 0.112, y 0.020; it is not used, and only the front lock's key scores. Under the near handle hangs the rear wall of the near trolley's basket, a steel wire grid in the plane x 0.180 from y -0.09 to 0.19: horizontal 5 mm rails at 0.270, 0.155 and 0.040 m over the bench and 8 upright 5 mm wires 40 mm apart. A rubber mat 100 x 100 x 3 mm lies on the bench centred at x 0.060, y -0.120. Both arms start in the ready pose. Real hardware: the near lock is printed from cad/coinlock.scad (dimensions checked against this scene by test_trolley.py; parts, print and assembly in cad/BUILD.md), the keys are cut from 3 mm stainless, the springs and screws are catalogue parts.
scoring: Stages, from the end state. 0.25: the front lock's key is in the near lock's slot, in line (its tip within 4 mm of the slot centre across and within 2.5 mm up or down, the key within 15 degrees of the slot's axis, tip first) and its tip 5 mm to 20 mm past the slot mouth (deeper means behind the lock, not in the slot). 0.5: also the coin slide out 35 mm or more of its 40 mm travel, and the key held by the lock: its tip 11.5 mm or more past the mouth with the lock's retaining pin dropped into the key's hole (within 1.5 mm of its rest, so it overlaps the key's thickness by 1 mm or more), so the key does not come out when pulled. The lock lets the slide out only when the key's tip has gone 12.5 mm past the mouth; a finger fits short of that. 0.75: also the quarter lying flat on the mat (its faces within 15 degrees of level, its centre 5 mm or more inside the mat's edges and its lowest point within 3 mm of the mat's top); a quarter standing on its edge does not count. 1.0: also the quarter, key, plunger and slide at rest (points under 0.01 m/s, spins under 0.5 rad/s) and every gripper point 30 mm or more from the key and the quarter, held for 1 s. Any state without the key in line and 5 mm in scores 0, so prying at the coin slide or reaching for the coin without the key scores 0; a key reversed or pushed in beside the slot scores 0. Real trial, on the printed lock of cad/ (same slot, plunger, pin and slide dimensions as the sim): a ruler on the key's exposed length (49.5 mm of blade outside the face when the tip is 12.5 mm in) and on the slide's travel, a 1 N pull on the key's chain for the retention, and a photo of the mat and the hands.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the retaining pin (on the real lock, a 1.5 mm wire pushed up through the release hole under the lock), pull the key out, put the quarter back in the slide and push the slide home until it latches. Let the key hang still on its chain.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; lock, quarter, nesting gap and tube at catalogue size. The lock follows EP0427819B1 loosely (a sprung tooth latches the slide out; a sprung pin in the key's hole stands in for its ball); the real one is printed to the sim's dimensions (cad/), its spring rates differ, and a wire hole releases its key. The chain is 11 rigid links, 40 mm short of the listing; the handles are shortened and lowered. Of the baskets only the near rear wall is modelled, not the child seat or front basket.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (on an earlier version of this scene, see README); scripted demo: 1.0
